Search terms for this lesson“how do I test a boss with friends and wire winning and dying?”Outline only

First, finish the two endings: what happens when the boss reaches 0 HP, and clean verification when StatManager.Die() triggers. Then swap seats and let friends playtest your entire boss fight cold — zero coaching allowed while they play.

Break It Down~10 minOutline only

Make both winning and losing real, then have friends playtest your boss blind and log every surprise.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Wire the victory payoff on boss defeat and verify StatManager.Die() resetwhat does this part do?Read: 5.3 (StatManager.Die() resetting health, halving coins, and calling LoadScene(current.name))
  2. Run a hands-off friend playtest and separate confusion, bugs, and balance noteswhat does this part do?Read: 7.7 / Playtest protocol below (silent observation + top-3 triage)

You already know how to beat your own boss because you wrote the timers and placed every platform. Your friends do not. Watching two classmates play silently without you explaining a single rule exposes unclear doors, hidden hitboxes, and soft-locks faster than another hour of solo tweaking.

Your turn

Pick two of the parts above and say in one line what each one actually does.

When the boss dies (health <= 0), why should victory drop an interactive goal (itemDrop, door opening, or Victory UI panel) instead of instantly destroying the player or leaving them trapped in a locked room?

Look at StatManager.Die(): if a player dies to your boss and SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name) reloads the arena, what happens to any coins or Double Jump unlock (maxJumps) stored on StatManager?

In the Code + Editor: Wire Win & Lose Cleanly (~20 min) ~20 min
OutcomeWhat Must HappenHow Your Project Already Supports It
Player Dies Player restarts outside or at the boss room start with full HP and all hazards reset. StatManager.Die() restores health = maxHealth, halves coins, and calls SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name).
Boss Dies Boss stops firing, clears active hazards cleanly, and reveals an exit, treasure drop, or Victory screen. EnemyController.Die() spawns itemDrop (e.g. trophy, portal, SceneSwitch, or Victory Canvas trigger) before calling Destroy(gameObject).
Replay Player can play again (returning to Start (index 0) or re-entering Overworld) without restarting Unity. SceneSwitch or a Play Again button calling SceneManager.LoadScene(0) resets cleanly while keeping one StatManager.

Socratic: Closing Both Ends of the Fight

  1. If your boss uses child Turret objects attached to the wall rather than children of the boss GameObject, destroying the boss leaves wall turrets still shooting during Victory! How do you turn them off cleanly in Die()?
  2. Suppose a player dies during your boss fight with coins = 5. After StatManager.Die() runs, what value does coinText display — and does StatManager.Die() currently update coinText.text inside Die() or only healthText.text?
  3. Where does a SceneSwitch (or Victory UI) go after the boss dies so a tester knows the game is beaten without asking you?
Studio: Blind Friend Playtesting (~40 min) ~40 min

Have two friends play your build back-to-back while you sit beside them with a notebook. Follow the strict silence rule:

  1. Hands off & mouth closed: start from Start (index 0) or your cave checkpoint and tell them only the keys if nothing on screen explains them — then say NOTHING for the next 3 minutes.
  2. Record observations, not excuses: never say "oh yeah, ignore that bug" or "you were supposed to jump there." Write down the exact frame or spot where they got stuck, died unfairly, or missed how to hurt the boss.
  3. Ask three questions after they finish (or die 3 times): (a) When did you know you were hurting the boss? (b) Which attack felt unfair or invisible? (c) Did you understand what happened when you won or died?

Socratic: Turning Playtest Notes Into Revisions

  1. Name one thing BOTH testers struggled with that surprised you — why did it feel obvious to you while building, and what changed when someone saw it cold?
  2. Look at your notes and sort every item into three buckets: Confusion (did not know what to do), Bug (broken collider/null error/soft-lock), or Balance (too easy / too fast). Which bucket breaks the game fastest?
  3. What if a friend suggested adding a whole new second boss — why do good developers prioritize clarity and fairness fixes on what exists rather than starting from scratch right before deadline?

Socratic: Verifying the Reset Loop

  1. During friend playtesting, what happened on try #2 after your tester died to the boss — did everything reset cleanly cleanly without stuck triggers or double HUDs?
  2. Did your friend reach the Victory outcome on their own, or only after asking you where the exit/goal was?
  3. Pick the TOP TWO concrete revisions you will execute next class before Freeze & Showcase.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Complete both victory (reward/portal/screen on boss defeat) and loss (StatManager.Die() clean reset)
  • Observe two friends playtesting your boss cold without coaching them
  • Categorize playtest notes into Confusion, Bugs, and Balance and pick top revisions
  • Commit and push
